quest.title: A Hero's Rite
quest.description: Having arrived at the Scions of the Canopy, you meet the young girl you helped before, Huni...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x425, Mora x34075, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x7

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: Huni! What were you thinking, going out by yourself? Don't you know how dangerous it is?

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: It's okay, Toba helped me, and... we met some kind strangers who helped us, and—

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: "Kind strangers"? What made you so sure they were so kind, hmm? I suppose they had "kind stranger" written on their foreheads?

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: Y—Yeah, actually, they did! In big bold letters!

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: Don't talk back to me! The Mountain King problem still hasn't been solved... What would I do if I lost you too? No dinner for you tonight!

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: They were good people, dad! Dinner or no dinner...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hello again, Huni!

dialogues.speaker: Huni
dialogues.text: #Ah, it's Miss Paimon and {M#Mr.}{F#Miss} {NICKNAME}! Dad, it's them! They're the ones who helped me... and I promised we'd take care of them if they came to visit...

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: Oh? So you're the "kind strangers," well...

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: I'm Trinidad. Apparently, you helped my daughter today, so if there's anything you need, just ask. As an elder of the Scions of the Canopy, I've got some influence around here.

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: Now, I trust that you're sensible people, who know better than to take advantage of their host's generosity.

choices.text: We just happened to be passing by, so we lent her a hand. It was nothing.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yep! Just helping a neighbor. We're not looking for anything in return.

response.speaker: Trinidad
response.text: Oh? Well, let's hope so...

response.speaker: Huni
response.text: Dad, please! They're not bad people! They've eaten at the same table with Kinich before. Be nice to them...

response.speaker: Trinidad
response.text: Kinich? Wait...

response.speaker: Trinidad
response.text: I heard that two mysterious travelers from afar showed up at the Stadium of the Sacred Flame. Are they... you?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Yes, I'm one of them.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And Paimon's the other!

response.speaker: Trinidad
response.text: Ah... Ahem...

response.speaker: Trinidad
response.text: ...I do apologize. A lot's been going on in our tribe lately, and I suppose the pressure must be getting to me, hehe... I can't believe I was so rude to you, I feel ashamed... *sigh* We got off on the wrong foot. Can we... start over?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, now we're talking! Seriously though, don't worry about it — already forgotten. We're just happy to see Huni got home safe and sound.

response.speaker: Trinidad
response.text: You've just arrived, I take it? It would be my honor to give you a hero's welcome tonight.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Careful now, that's quite an about-face... We've heard that kind of thing can lead to spontaneous combustion around these parts.

response.speaker: Trinidad
response.text: *cough*

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Save the VIP treatment. If you need a favor, let's talk.

response.speaker: Trinidad
response.text: Hah... My dear Traveler, you are very perceptive indeed!

response.speaker: Trinidad
response.text: Go inside now, Huni. Dad's got some important business to discuss.

response.speaker: Huni
response.text: #Okay. Look after {M#Mr.}{F#Miss} {NICKNAME} and Miss Paimon, they're very special guests!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, we'll hear you out, but we can't make any promises that we'll be able to help.

response.speaker: Trinidad
response.text: Ahem... This is a matter of utmost importance. Please, allow me to explain...

response.speaker: Trinidad
response.text: For many years, our tribe has celebrated the Turnfire Night. It is a traditional ceremony among the Scions of the Canopy, in which we remember our ancestor, Burkina, and his companion, Kongamato the Mountain King.

response.speaker: Trinidad
response.text: Burkina was a hero who bore the ancient name Mal{RUBY#[D]Turnfire}ipo, and Kongamato was a powerful yumkasaur warrior. Together, they fought against the Abyss.

response.speaker: Trinidad
response.text: They were victorious, but it came at a great cost... Burkina paid with his life. The Mountain King survived, but was contaminated by the Abyss, and he remains in hibernation to this day.

response.speaker: Trinidad
response.text: Normally, yumkasaurs never live longer than a century. It's possible that the Abyssal power is responsible for his unnaturally long lifespan.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Wait, so he's still alive?

response.speaker: Trinidad
response.text: That's right. The Mountain King is a living symbol of our glory, but even this glory comes at a price.

response.speaker: Trinidad
response.text: The Abyssal power inside him is highly sensitive, and when it is disturbed, he awakens and flies into a blind rage, attacking anything that moves...

response.speaker: Trinidad
response.text: So, besides the ceremony, another important part of Turnfire Night each year is cleansing the Abyssal power inside the Mountain King, so that he will remain sound asleep.

response.speaker: Trinidad
response.text: However, Abyss-related incidents have been on the rise in Natlan lately, as I'm sure you're both aware. As a result, it has become increasingly difficult to keep the Mountain King in hibernation.

response.speaker: Trinidad
response.text: Only five months have passed since the last Turnfire Night, and he's already showing signs of instability.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Has he woken up again?

response.speaker: Trinidad
response.text: He has. We managed to contain the situation by performing a makeshift ceremony right away, but it was a close call. He could reawaken at any moment.

response.speaker: Trinidad
response.text: Also, he attacked and wounded my companion, Nanna, during the ceremony... She became contaminated by the Abyss as a result, and...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We heard... Such a tragedy. We're really sorry for your loss.

response.speaker: Trinidad
response.text: *sigh*... Yes, and Nanna wasn't the first...

response.speaker: Trinidad
response.text: Anyway, right now we're preparing for an exceptional Turnfire Night ceremony, and we need to find a suitable flame bearer. From what I've heard about your adventures, I believe you'd be perfect for the role.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Don't you already have a flame bearer in the tribe?

response.speaker: Trinidad
response.text: Of course. Plus, he's a bona-fide hero who's inherited the Mal{RUBY#[D]Turnfire}ipo name.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, you mean Kinich!

response.speaker: Trinidad
response.text: Yes, he's the one. A hero worth his weight in gold — and unfortunately for us, he's all too aware of that... No prizes for guessing what he said when I asked him to host a Turnfire Night outside of the annual schedule.

response.speaker: Trinidad
response.text: "An exceptional ceremony? I'll have to charge an exceptional price." I swear, no other concept exists in that boy's brain...

choices.text: At least he's predictable. Fork over the Mora, and he's all yours.

response.speaker: Trinidad
response.text: I'm not the one to usually talk about people behind their backs, but I'm convinced the Wayob got hit on the head and took a wrong turn the day it chose to give that ancient name to him. Have you ever heard of a hero whose mantra is "What's your asking price"?

response.speaker: Trinidad
response.text: Oh, and don't get me started on that insufferable Ajaw he hangs around with. Thinks he's god's gift to mankind! Pompous fool...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah... Paimon has to agree on that last part!

response.speaker: Trinidad
response.text: Anyway, the fact is, the ceremony can just as easily be done without him as long as we find someone else — and besides, you two seem like much better candidates. Hehe... So, what do you think?

choices.text: Just tell me what I need to do next.

response.speaker: Trinidad
response.text: Wonderful! I can't thank you enough. Huni was right about you — you have kindness in your hearts.

response.speaker: Trinidad
response.text: Come with me to the other side of the mountain. I'll bring you up to speed on each step of the ceremony. As experienced warriors, I'm sure you'll pick it up in no time.

response.speaker: Trinidad
response.text: You will gain the respect and friendship of the Scions of the Canopy. Something no amount of Mora can buy.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sounds good. It's a deal.

choices.text: Why don't I try to talk some sense into Kinich for you?

response.speaker: Trinidad
response.text: There's only a few days left before the ceremony — we can't afford to waste what little time we have on negotiating with him. I'd much prefer if you would consider taking his place.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Alright, guess there's no other choice.

choices.text: Sounds like a professional adventurer to me.
Of course. All we ask for is one million Mora.

response.speaker: Trinidad
response.text: One million Mora!? Hahaha! At least you're a straight-shooter. I can respect that much.

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Achoo! Curses! Who dares insult the Great K'uhul Ajaw behind his back?

dialogues.speaker: Sanka
dialogues.text: Oh, Great K'uhul Ajaw! Bless you!

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Shut your filthy mouth, worm of the Abyss! Your putrid words defile the air we breathe! You make the Almighty Dragonlord, K'uhul Ajaw sick to the stomach!

dialogues.speaker: Sanka
dialogues.text: Speaking as a member of the Abyss Order, that's music to my ears — exactly the kind of reaction we're going for. But on a personal level, I gotta say, it's pretty hurtful.

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Never have we heard such brazen blustering from someone who is inches from death! Up yours, four-eyes! We spit in your face! *spitting sounds*

dialogues.speaker: Sanka
dialogues.text: Okay, well THAT I am at a loss to explain. How do I manage to stay so chirpy and cheerful? I can only guess it's some kind of powerful magic...

dialogues.speaker: Sanka
dialogues.text: But I digress. Mr. Kinich, I admit it — you, Sir, are a legendary hunter. Still, the only reason you caught me is that I was reluctant to run away.

dialogues.speaker: Sanka
dialogues.text: You see, I'm very interested in the lore of your tribe.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Kay.

dialogues.speaker: Sanka
dialogues.text: ...Is that it? "'Kay"? Aren't you intrigued to know what it is about you guys that prompted a visit from the Abyss?

dialogues.speaker: Sanka
dialogues.text: It's the extreme sports! The other day, I narrowly avoided getting hit by a very brave soul who'd just leaped off a cliff... I think you call it "bungee jumping"? Anyway, I was very impressed! That is what I call embracing the spirit of adventure!

dialogues.speaker: Sanka
dialogues.text: Look, I even did a painting inspired by the bravery and freedom of the Scions of the Canopy...

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: You scum-sucking swine! I swear, if you go bungee jumping, it'll be without a rope!

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Head-first off the tallest cliff, with a band of hunters on your tail! And nowhere left to run! And a bottomless cesspit waiting for you on the ground!

dialogues.speaker: Sanka
dialogues.text: You say that, but I get the sense that Mr. Kinich isn't planning to take my life right now. On top of that, I'm tired of spying on you from afar... So why don't we just negotiate a comfortable operating distance that works for both of us?

dialogues.speaker: Sanka
dialogues.text: I've heard that the most important thing in human relationships is to respect each other's boundaries. What do you say, Mr. Kinich?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Or... you could tell me what it is you're really after.

dialogues.speaker: Sanka
dialogues.text: Wha...?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: And then I'll name my price.

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: Ugh, the Abyss contamination is back... No surprises there. No doubt that explains the Mountain King's recent activity.

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: See those torches over there? Those are sacred flame offshoots that we requested from the Stadium of the Sacred Flame. They contain the power of the Pyro Archon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you saying that the Sacred Flame and the Turnfire are the same thing?

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: Heh, for ceremonial purposes, at least. Sending someone to the Night Kingdom to retrieve the legendary Turnfire isn't exactly an option. More to the point though, the Sacred Flame is able to burn away Abyssal filth, so that's why we use it in the ceremony.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Gotcha... So basically, we just need to clean up the filth with the Sacred Flame?

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: That's one part of it, yes. But the complete ceremony is a bit more complicated than that.

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: First, the flame bearer must collect a kindling of the Sacred Flame from the starting point, then use a grappling hook to fly up into the sky and light each of the Sacred Flame Pillars.

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: Then, they must go down into the canyon, all the way to the cave where the Mountain King slumbers, lighting braziers and the final altar along the way.

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: The most skilled flame bearers can accomplish all of this without touching the ground once. As much as I hate to admit it, Kinich is capable of this.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, he can do all that flying without ever falling to the ground?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So can you, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, of course Paimon can! It'd be much harder for you guys.

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: Haha, well, don't worry — it's not a requirement of the ceremony. You're allowed to touch the ground. The only thing you're not allowed to do is turn back.

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: The flame bearer must always keep moving forward. You can't skip a pillar, then come back to it after lighting the next one. To do so would be to disrespect our ancestors.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So... What actually happens if you do turn back? Surely the fires don't just go out?

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: Umm... Well, if you're not careful, you might get burned.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What about today, then? Does the same rule apply?

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: Oh no, don't worry. Today is just a practice, the order doesn't matter. You just need to take the sacred flame, cleanse the filth, then go light all the braziers.

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: Are you ready?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's begin.

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: I'll repeat the key points again. Gather the kindling, cleanse the filth, and light all the braziers. I'll wait for you at the end.

talks.objective: Obtain kindling from the Sacred Flame

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: I knew I was right about you. You have outperformed all of our previous candidates.

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: If there's an Ancient Name for outstanding flame bearers, I'm sure the Wayob would consider you for the honor.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Paimon could probably get the job done, too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah! Although, it would probably take Paimon quite a bit longer...

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: Haha. Alright, now there's still a few days left until the ceremony. I should probably get back so I can inform the chief and the other elders that I have found the flame bearer we need.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh... You mean, they've still got to sign off on it?

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: Some of them are still hoping we can come to an agreement with Kinich. But that's only because they haven't seen you in action.

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: Still, I'm the one responsible for securing a flame bearer, and my recommendation is you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Just for Paimon's own peace of mind, are you sure it's not gonna be a problem having outlanders take on such an important role in your ceremony?

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: See that place over there? There was a time, long before the age of Burkina and the Mountain King, when we Scions of the Canopy called that our home.

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: After a period of upheaval, our ancestors were forced to move away. Now, it has become a place where our youths go to develop courage and kindle a spirit of adventure.

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: If we fail to keep the threat posed by the Mountain King at bay, it might not be long before we have to move again, and find a new home...

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: So, to answer your question, I think everyone will agree that you are the right choice.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Fair enough. Desperate times call for desperate measures...

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: I'll need you to drop by my place at some point before the ceremony, if that's alright. There are still a few final details that we need to discuss.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, see you later then!

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: You have my gratitude.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We've helped out with a lot of other local festivals before, but this one feels a little different... Anyway, let's take a break before heading back to Trinidad's place.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Meanwhile, in a hidden cave...
